timeline.title: One point short in 2018, Ahvar Rizvi gets his Asian Games chance eight years later
timeline.description: One point short of India’s 2018 Asian Games selection, Trap shooter Ahvar Rizvi spent the next seven years rebuilding his career after Double Trap was removed from the international programme. The 2018 junior world champion struggled with the transition, briefly quit shooting and later competed with teammate Lakshya Sheoran’s gun. Now, Rizvi has made his first Asian Games team and is preparing to represent India in Trap at Nagoya.

timeline.title: Asian Games: Sindhu, Hooda exits cap India's disappointing badminton campaign
timeline.description: At the Asian Games 2026, India's badminton team concluded with just one medal. Both PV Sindhu and Unnati Hooda exited in the women's singles quarterfinals after fierce competition. The women’s doubles team fell to a strong Malaysian pair, and mixed doubles suffered a narrow defeat. A demanding tournament schedule took its toll on performance, highlighting a stark decline from their previous edition's achievements.

timeline.title: Sujeet Kalkal on turning Olympic heartbreak into Asian Games gold
timeline.description: Sujeet Kalkal's Asian Games gold came two years after floods in Dubai cost him a chance to qualify for the Paris Olympics. The 25-year-old wrestler fought back from 2-9 down to beat Tajikistan's Abdulmazhid Kudiev 10-9 in the 65kg final, ending India's eight-year wait for a wrestling gold at the Games. Now targeting Los Angeles 2028, Kalkal says he does not want to go to the Olympics just to participate - he wants gold.

issues.brief_summary: India and Switzerland have signed five agreements covering migration, mobility, transport, research and technology.
